issues.legal_issue: The succession rules in force when a female life-estate holder dies govern succession to the estate of a Hindu male who died intestate before those rules came into force.
material_facts: The last male owner held the property absolutely and died intestate before the succession reform came into force.
His mother held the property for life and died after the reform came into force; his sister then held the property for life and died later.
The claimant was the last male owner's sister's son, while the competing claimant was his paternal uncle.
The courts found that the property was not coparcenary property and had not been disposed of by will.
issues.conclusion: The succession opened when the female life estate terminated, so the reform applied notwithstanding that the last male owner had died earlier. The sister's son was preferred to the paternal uncle, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Hindu Law of Inheritance (Amendment) Act, 1929, section 1(2), the Act applies to Mitakshara separate property not held in coparcenary and not disposed of by will; section 3 places the specified relations, including a sister's son, ahead of a paternal uncle. Following Lala Duni Chand v. Musammat Anar Kali, the relevant time is when succession opens on termination of the female life estate, not the earlier death of the male owner. The Court also relied on Annagouda Nathgouda Patil v. Court of Wards for the Act's scope and referred to Shrimati Shakuntala Devi v. Kaushalya Devi, Rajpali Kunwar v. Sarju Rai, Pokhan Dusadh v. Mst. Manoa, Lakshmi v. Anantharama, and Bindeshari Singh v. Baij Nath Singh in support of when succession opens. The earlier contrary views in Krishnan Chettiar v. Manikammal and Kanhaiya Lal v. Mst. Champa Devi had been overruled by later Full Bench decisions.

rule.if: civil_succession_appeal and male_owner_died_intestate and property_was_separate and property_was_not_willed and succession_reform_was_in_force_when_life_estate_ended and claimant_is_sisters_son and competing_heir_is_paternal_uncle

predicates.civil_succession_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning competing claims to succeed to a deceased person's estate.
predicates.male_owner_died_intestate: The last male owner died without leaving a will.
predicates.property_was_separate: The property belonged separately to the last male owner and was not held in coparcenary.
predicates.property_was_not_willed: The last male owner did not dispose of the property by will.
predicates.succession_reform_was_in_force_when_life: The succession reform was in force when the female holder's life estate ended.
predicates.claimant_is_sisters_son: The claimant is the sister's son of the last male owner.
predicates.competing_heir_is_paternal_uncle: The competing heir is the last male owner's paternal uncle.

issues.definition: When a succession appeal concerns separate, unwilled property of an intestate male and the female life estate ends after the succession reform is in force, a claimant who is the male owner's sister's son is preferred to a competing paternal uncle.

issues.legal_issue: When a female life estate ends after the succession reform has come into force, the last male owner's sister may succeed in her own right as a preferential heir and take a life estate.
material_facts: The last male owner died intestate, and his mother held the property for life.
The mother's life estate ended after the succession reform had come into force.
The last male owner's sister was the next female holder of the property, and the Court stated that she succeeded as a preferential heir, though her interest was itself a life estate.
issues.conclusion: Succession could be treated as having opened when the mother's life estate ended, at which point the sister succeeded in her own right as a preferential heir with a life estate.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that the sister's succession could be regarded as opening on termination of the mother's life estate and that the sister succeeded under section 3(b) of the Hindu Law of Inheritance (Amendment) Act, 1929, with only a life estate. This statement was made although the point had not been raised by the parties.

predicates.male_owner_died_intestate: The last male owner died without leaving a will.
predicates.female_life_estate_ended_after_reform: A female holder's life estate ended after the succession reform came into force.
predicates.claimant_is_sister_of_last_male_owner: The person claiming through the ended life estate is the last male owner's sister.

issues.definition: If an intestate male owner's female life estate ends after the succession reform is in force and his sister is the claimant, the sister succeeds with a life estate.
